learner_notice: Feedback follows a committed response. The opening activity is informational; an unresolved fresh check returns to planning without credit.

items.title: Starting check: direct access
items.prompt: A transit-board memo quotes a maintenance engineer who inspected several rail joints that morning. Which passage-supplied detail most directly strengthens the engineer's credibility about whether those joints were cracked?
options: The memo places the engineer's quotation in its opening paragraph
The engineer personally inspected the rail joints named in the claim
The engineer describes the inspection in a calm, formal sentence
The board prints the statement beneath an official agency seal
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Guided practice: relevant records
items.prompt: A museum report compares a conservator who maintains twelve years of humidity logs with a donor who says one gallery felt damp during a visit. Who is better positioned to support a claim about the gallery's long-term humidity pattern?
options: The donor, because financial support gives broad authority over the gallery
The donor, because a visitor has fewer institutional duties than an employee
The museum director, because the highest title is always most credible
The conservator, because the relevant role and longitudinal records fit the claim
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Less help: source for timing
items.prompt: A passage asks when barriers first blocked a neighborhood road. A resident says she watched workers place them at 6 a.m.; a regional economist explains how closures can affect commerce. Which source is more credible for the timing claim?
options: The resident, because the passage gives her direct observation of the placement
The economist, because regional analysis covers more locations than one witness
The economist, because economic expertise determines when barriers were installed
Both sources equally, because every quoted source has the same access
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: On your own: interest and corroboration
items.prompt: A manufacturer-paid consultant reports that a filter removed 82% of a test contaminant. The passage also says two independent laboratories reproduced nearly the same result. Which evaluation is best supported?
options: The payment proves the reported removal rate is false
The independent tests erase every possible concern about objectivity
The payment raises an objectivity concern, while corroboration supports the result
The consultant's technical title makes the independent tests irrelevant
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: purchasing audit
items.prompt: A school-lunch audit says a dietitian analyzed six months of purchase records, while the principal offers a general assurance that meals are balanced. For a claim about how often whole grains were purchased, which evaluation is strongest?
options: The principal is stronger because administrative rank establishes nutritional expertise
The dietitian is stronger because relevant expertise is paired with the cited records
The principal is stronger because a confident assurance is direct evidence
The sources are equal because both work for the same school system
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: mixed cues
items.prompt: An editorial quotes a beekeeper who reports fewer hive visits near a proposed construction site. The beekeeper sells honey from those hives, and the passage also cites a university count showing a smaller decline. Which judgment best evaluates the beekeeper's claim?
options: The financial stake makes the observation unusable regardless of other evidence
Direct observation makes the claim fully reliable despite the disclosed stake
The university count proves the beekeeper fabricated the larger decline
Direct access supports the report, while stake and partial corroboration limit confidence
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: test relevant access
items.prompt: Which question most directly tests whether a represented source has relevant access and expertise for a passage claim?
options: Did this source observe or work with the event and evidence named in the claim?
Does this source use the longest and most detailed sentence in the passage?
Is this source introduced before every other person quoted by the author?
Would readers probably agree with this source's conclusion outside the passage?
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: assay records
items.prompt: A water-quality summary quotes a laboratory technician who ran the named blinded assays and a mayor who says the water looks clear. For a claim about the assay results, whose credibility is better supported by the passage?
options: The mayor's, because elected office grants authority over every technical result
The mayor's, because visual clarity is equivalent to a blinded chemical assay
The technician's, because direct work with the assays fits the specific claim
Both equally, because the summary presents each statement as a quotation
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: calibrate a disclosed stake
items.prompt: When a passage discloses that a source may benefit from a claim, what is the most defensible next step?
options: Accept the claim if the source also speaks from direct experience
Treat the stake as one cue and compare the source's support and corroboration
Reject the claim before considering any records or independent observations
Ignore the stake whenever the source has a professional title
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: advocacy and documents
items.prompt: A preservation advocate says a theater is the city's oldest surviving venue. The passage notes the advocate's campaign role and cites dated permits and photographs that support the construction year. Which evaluation is best?
options: The campaign role proves the historical claim was invented
The dated records make the advocate's role irrelevant to source evaluation
Advocacy makes the claim less credible than any unsupported opposing statement
Advocacy warrants caution, while the cited documents provide specific support
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Starting check: stance word
items.prompt: A columnist writes that the board 'recklessly delayed the repair.' Which word most clearly signals the columnist's stance toward the delay?
options: recklessly
board
delayed
repair
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Guided practice: certainty and praise
items.prompt: A report says, 'The council wisely rejected the plan,' but supplies only the vote total. Which analysis best links the wording to reliability?
options: Council is a stance word because it names the group that voted
Rejected is unreliable because every negative verb proves bias
Wisely praises the decision beyond what the vote total alone establishes
Plan is unreliable because the sentence does not describe its length
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Less help: calibrated hedge
items.prompt: A study summary reports a small association and says the exposure 'may contribute' to the outcome. What reliability effect is most plausible from that phrase alone?
options: It proves the author doubts every measurement in the study
It can align the claim's certainty with limited correlational evidence
It turns the association into a demonstrated causal mechanism
It removes the need to examine the evidence supplied in the summary
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: On your own: absolute claim
items.prompt: After interviewing twelve volunteers, an essay states that the program 'always transforms participants into confident leaders.' Which reliability judgment is strongest?
options: The claim is reliable because confident language signals strong evidence
The claim is false because every absolute statement is necessarily fabricated
The sample size is irrelevant because the sentence describes participants
The absolute wording extends beyond what the limited interview sample supports
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: dismissive framing
items.prompt: An author writes, 'Only a careless observer could accept the alternative explanation,' then presents no evidence against that alternative. How does the phrasing affect reliability?
options: It weakens reliability by dismissing an alternative through a label rather than evidence
It strengthens reliability because careless identifies a likely source of error
It has no effect because the sentence does not include a numerical claim
It proves the alternative explanation is correct and the author knows it
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: paired accounts
items.prompt: Two accounts describe the same meeting. Account A says protesters 'finally forced a sensible delay' and omits the safety inspection. Account B reports the delay, notes the inspection, and says the cause remains uncertain. Which comparison is best supported?
options: Account A is fully reliable because it states a clear cause for the delay
Account B is unreliable because uncertainty always signals weak research
Account A's certainty and omission weaken it relative to Account B
Both accounts are equally reliable because they agree that a delay occurred
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: phrase and effect
items.prompt: Which method most directly repairs an incomplete statement that a passage 'sounds biased'?
options: Identify the author's background and predict which opinions that identity usually produces
Quote the operative phrase, restate it neutrally, and name the framing change
Decide whether the stance matches your own reaction to the issue
Count every adjective and treat the passage with more adjectives as false
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: public-safety wording
items.prompt: A safety notice calls a competing proposal 'a flashy distraction' without comparing its cost or effectiveness. What is the most direct reliability effect of that wording?
options: The notice becomes reliable because memorable wording improves comprehension
The proposal must be effective because the notice criticizes it
The phrase has no effect unless the notice identifies the proposal's author
The label discourages consideration without supplying a comparison that warrants dismissal
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: bias and factual support
items.prompt: Which rule best separates evidence of biased framing from a judgment that a factual claim is false?
options: Evaluate the framing cue and the factual support as related but distinct questions
Treat every openly committed source as factually wrong before reading its evidence
Ignore selective language whenever one numerical detail appears in the passage
Accept any factual claim whose wording sounds neutral and unemotional
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: advocacy report
items.prompt: An advocacy report accurately lists 48 completed repairs but calls the program 'an unquestioned triumph' and omits that 70 repairs were scheduled. Which evaluation is most defensible?
options: The celebratory phrase proves the count of 48 was fabricated
The exact count makes the omitted schedule and evaluative wording irrelevant
The count may be accurate, while the language and omission overstate overall success
The report is fully neutral because it includes at least one numerical detail
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.
